title: fleet-bootstrap-validation-and-hardware-quirks-playbook
body:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook for fleet bootstrap validation across mixed bare-metal and vSphere on-prem fleets. Focus is early lifecycle: preflight validation, hardware quirks discovery and mitigation patterns, Terraform module notes for machine-sets and BMC/IPMI wiring, and a conservative cluster upgrade/rollback plan. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — notes to self and checklist style.

Audience: field engineers, SREs, solutions eng, cust success who touch on-prem installs.

High-level goals:
- Ensure repeatable validation steps that catch the most common failure classes before kubeadm/kubelet install.
- Capture vendor/hardware quirks we see in lab (Dell, HPE, Supermicro) and simple mitigations that don't require custom OS images.
- Provide Terraform module expectations and a minimal example for the provisioning path we use in the private product.
- Describe a low-risk cluster upgrade plan tuned for fleets with mixed GPU and non-GPU nodes.

Quick TL;DR checklist (pre-OS image):
- Serial console access verified (BMC creds + out-of-band reachability).
- NIC ordering validated (PXE NIC -> management NIC mapping).
- RAID/BIOS set to AHCI / SATA mode where possible; disable secure boot if custom kernels.
- Verify TPM presence and policy — if TPM required, ensure KMS integration note handled later.
- kdump/tnet disabled if kernel crash handlers interfere with live migration tests.
- Power cycling test: verify IPMI power on/off delays < 30s and node power state transitions stable.
- Disk health: SMART quick test pass, consistent model numbers for expected performance tier.
- NVMe namespace mapping consistent across reboots for hugepages & pmem use-cases.

Common hardware quirks & mitigations (lab-observed):
- Quirk: NIC reorder after BIOS update on some Supermicro boards.
  - Mitigation: Lock MAC->device mapping in udev (udev-rule template attached below), use bioscfg to pin boot NIC. Documented as step in preflight.
- Quirk: RAID controller firmware resets disks to RAID0 on first init on certain chassis models.
  - Mitigation: Run controller health and controller-init script in pre-image validation job; require firmware level >= tested-minimum.
- Quirk: BMCs with aggressive network timeouts drop SOL (serial over lan) during long uploads.
  - Mitigation: Use rsync/mtu tuning or chunked firmware pushes and keep a local cache in field-worker.
- Quirk: vSphere ephemeral NIC naming differs when nested virtualization is used.
  - Mitigation: Rely on vSphere UUID in terraform provider mapping rather than guest OS device name.

Preflight automated tests (recommend running in lab before field run):
1) IPMI reachability: ipmitool lan print, ipmitool chassis status.
2) NIC baseline latency test: run 30s ping between node and gateway; check drops <1% over interval.
3) Disk performance: fio profile with 4k/64k mixed read/write for 60s to validate tiers.
4) Kernel boot test: boot to target kernel and test module load paths (nv_peer_mem, vfio).
5) Kubelet conformance smoke: run kubelet --version and kubeadm preflight bundle to ensure expected runtime flags parsed.

Terraform module notes (opinionated, for infra/cluster provisioning):
- Module boundaries: keep hardware provisioning (ipmi, bmc, vlan assignment) in one module, OS image & ignition attachment in a second module, and k8s nodegroup provisioning in a third. This allows reusing the same machine-set across different images/ignitions without reprovisioning BMC slots.
- State handling: Use per-rack or per-room backend key prefixes to reduce locking hotspots in S3/GCS.
- Example var contract (copy-paste friendly):
  - var "rack_id" { type = string }
  - var "bmc_address" { type = string }
  - var "bmc_user" { type = string }
  - var "node_role" { type = string }
  - var "preferred_cpu_families" { type = list(string) }
- Resource naming: canonicalize to: redwood-${env}-${rack}-${hostname_short}. This prevents collisions when customers reuse hostnames.
- Idempotency notes: always use a tag on BMC-managed assets that includes a provisioning-run-id; Terraform should check tag to avoid re-initializing a device that was previously provisioned manually.
- Example snippet (pseudo-terraform):
  module "bmc_provision" {
    source = "../modules/bmc-provision"
    rack_id = var.rack_id
    bmc_address = var.bmc_address
    credentials = local.bmc_creds
  }

- Recommended provider versions: pin provider for ipmi / vsphere for the release we validated with (e.g., vsphere 2.x, ipmi 0.x depending on community version). Add upgrade notes in CHANGELOG of module.

Ignition/OS image considerations:
- Keep cloud-init/ignition minimal: prefer a two-step pattern where the base image only contains node-agent and minimal tooling; the second stage (controlled by bootstrap server) pulls tuned kube parameters. This helps rollback if an image introduces regression.
- Kernel cmdline: ensure cgroup v1 flags off and cgroup v2 enabled if using CRI that requires it. Document per-customer fallback.

Cluster bootstrap steps (recommended sequence):
1) Provision OS image and attach ignition; mark node in inventory as "standby".
2) Serial console sanity check and IPMI power cycle validation.
3) Run node preflight test bundle; only move to "provision" if passes.
4) Join node to cluster as unschedulable tainted (taint: node.kubernetes.io/bootstrap=true).
5) Run node-level e2e smoke tests (CRI, networking (CNI basic ping), ephemeral volume mount).
6) Remove taint and schedule systematically in waves defined by capacity SLOs.

Upgrade and rollback plan (control plane and kubelet):
- Upgrade approach: rolling control plane upgrade with control-plane nodes first, followed by worker nodes in waves. For mixed hardware, schedule GPU-heavy nodes in later waves.
- Canary strategy: pick 1 control-plane and 2 worker nodes (non-critical) as canaries. Run full test harness (api latency, scheduling, GPU job run) for 1h before proceeding.
- Kubelet/containerd: use cordon->drain->upgrade(daemonset/apt/yum/pipeline)->uncordon. For GPU nodes, drain with --ignore-daemonsets and watch for long-running jobs; if jobs are stateful, prefer maintenance window.
- Rollback criteria: API 5xx spike > 3x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes, or test harness failure. Rollback steps: revert kubeadm plan on control plane (kubeadm rollback doc refs), redeploy previous machine image for workers if kubelet regression.

Field run playbook (day-of checklist):
- Bring up a small staging cluster that mirrors customer network config and run the full preflight suite.
- Verify TLS cert provisioning path (vault/KMS) and ensure CSR automated step succeeds.
- Confirm NTP/time sync across BMC and hosts (unsynced clocks are a common install breaker).
- Validate cross-rack routing rules (avoid hairpin NAT in first-pass).

Troubleshooting snippets (cheat-sheet style):
- Node never joins cluster: check cloud-init logs (/var/log/cloud-init.log), check ignition stage-2 for permission errors.
- kubelet crashloop after upgrade: check kernel modules mismatch; roll back to previous kernel via grub entry.
- Disk UUID mismatch after image bake: run lsblk -f and match by model/serial or update fstab to use PARTUUID.

Open questions / TODOs:
- We need a standardized udev rule library per vendor to avoid per-customer ad-hoc fixes. Action: Maya to prototype and add to infra repo.
- Decide on default of secureboot: enabled for FIPS customers, but many GPU drivers require disabled secureboot. Need a per-customer policy flag surfaced in Terraform.
- Add an automated firmware validation pipeline in CI that tests common BMC/ipmi actions against lab hardware. (Ravi follow-up).

References and artifacts to copy into final playbook:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/324 (terraform module split proposal)
- JIRA: RDW-1189 (customer A on-prem install notes)
- Confluence page for hardware catalog (placeholder id: CON-4872)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally pragmatic — field teams don't need theoretical best-practice laundry list, they need likely-to-fail items called out with quick mitigations.
- When possible, prefer non-invasive mitigations (udev rules, ignition hooks) so we avoid vendor image rebuilds.

If this doc is useful, next steps: 1) convert the preflight checks into an executable test package (ansible/playbook). 2) Add a Terraform example in infra repo under examples/fleet-bootstrap. 3) Bake a minimal image that includes udev/firmware-helper scripts and pin BIOS/fw versions in catalog.

-- end of draft --
